description: The Soviet 40th Army conducts widespread sweeps against Mujahideen strongholds in the Hindu Kush, while foreign intelligence agencies funnel Stingers and logistics through ratlines.

committee.public_briefing: Delegates manage political, military, intelligence, and humanitarian responses during the Soviet-Afghan War. Crisis staff adjudicate directives and publish confirmed updates through the committee feed.
rules_of_engagement: All military actions require a written directive or explicit chair authorization.
Crisis staff may translate directives into morale, supply, fatigue, combat, or speed effects.
Intelligence is faction-limited unless chairs publish it as a public crisis update.
Humanitarian, diplomatic, and media actions can alter morale, supply, alliances, or public situation reports.

delegate_roles.role: Soviet Council of Ministers / 40th Army Command
delegate_roles.briefing: Balance military pressure, domestic cost, and regime stability.
Preserve state control, legitimacy, and coordination with Soviet forces.
Coordinate decentralized forces, preserve popular support, and exploit terrain.
Manage cross-border support, deniability, and regional spillover.

delegate_roles.role: National Security Council / Covert Action Cell
delegate_roles.briefing: Shape external support while managing escalation risk.
Protect border interests and influence aligned networks.

victory_conditions: Maintain or contest provincial influence without exhausting military readiness.
Protect faction legitimacy through public crisis updates and humanitarian posture.
Convert successful directives into durable diplomatic or operational advantages.
committee.staff_notes: Use adjudication effects conservatively: morale and supply shifts represent broad political/logistical outcomes, while combat/speed modifiers represent temporary staff rulings.
